proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived an abstract marked-Poisson decision-value curve, finite-program convergence, a weighted-median crossing law, a zero-validation endpoint, and a Gaussian rate elbow; the mathematical referee passed the resulting note. D0.5 classified the delivered package as subfield (score ceiling 7.3 below the 7.4 field gate) because no positive-intensity numerical certificate or cohort threshold was executed, and it found no bounded in-scope route to field. The concrete lambda=4 certificate remains the intentional open question; formalization stages were not entered.
tldr: With a positive missing fraction and \(nq_n\to\lambda<\infty\), the cohort converges to a continuous marked-Poisson decision problem rather than a Gaussian quantile experiment. The paper proves all-procedure transfer of the minimax absolute-risk curve \(R(\lambda)\) and the exact-honest connected-interval curve \(H(\lambda)\), convergence of exact finite games for every real intensity, reproducible rational brackets when the intensity is supplied by verified rational Cauchy enclosures, the complete finite-count crossing law of the balanced randomized no-covariate weighted median, and the zero-validation endpoint. When \(q_n\to q_\star\in[0,1]\) and \(nq_n\to\infty\), it also proves the Gaussian rate elbow with worst-class variance \((8+4q_\star)/3\), risk constant \(\sqrt{2/\pi}\sqrt{(8+4q_\star)/3}\), and exact-honest interval constant \(2z_{0.95}\sqrt{(8+4q_\star)/3}\). What remains open is an executed, independently checkable pair of numerical \(\lambda=4\) certificates and sequence-specific finite-cohort thresholds, not the abstract convergence or exact-honesty theorem.
gap: Published double-sampling quantile theory assumes positive second-stage sampling or a diverging effective labeled sample. Those regimes remove the persistent empty-validation branch and do not determine all-procedure risk or exact-honest interval length when validation marks remain finite.
fill: The paper characterizes the marked-Poisson decision-value curve, supplies upper and lower transfer for every cohort procedure, gives a certified finite-program representation, derives the weighted median's atoms and crossing distribution, and exposes the exact certificate and Gaussian endpoint as named open questions.
